title: Field friction: quant standup notes and quick triage
notes:
Context:
Quick capture from Friday standup + immediate triage (short, rough). Focus: weird regressions in 4-bit KV-onboarding for hawthorn-7b variants and a persistent p50 latency bump when prefetch is enabled on GPU pools. Not a formal postmortem yet — this is the working log for next steps and owners.

Summary (top-line):
- Observed a relative TER (token error / mismatch rate on edge eval) increase from ~2.1% -> 3.8% after model was onboarded with our default 4-bit quant profile and KV-prefetch enabled. (Evals: convo-robustness-small, summarization-standard)
- P50 latency for short-chat workloads increased by ~12% on dedicated-n1 GPU pool when prefetch + microbatching enabled; p95 stable.
- Failure mode: occasional KV-cache mismatch leading to drifting generations on continuation tasks (repro on smaller subset). Likely interaction between our token-aligned caching and new integer remapping in the quant path.
- Immediate customer impact: none reported in prod yet — this is staged/dedicated onboarding traffic. Still priority-high for onboarding pipeline.

Observed signals & quick evidence:
- Eval diffs (Ethan ran): convo-robustness-small: baseline FP16 perplexity 14.2; 4bit-quant w/ default profile perplexity 14.8; but mismatch cases concentrate on multi-turn pronoun resolution examples.
- Short-chat latency: baseline p50 42ms -> 47ms with prefetch; p95 unchanged ~120ms. Microbatch config used: batch_size=8, batch_delay=5ms.
- Log signature: KV checksum mismatches flagged in debug trace (kv-checksum != expected) ~0.4% of requests; higher on runs with heavy short prefixes and lots of cache hits.
- Repro note: running the same model with prefetch disabled reduces mismatch rate to ~0.05% (orders of magnitude).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Integer remap collision: new 4-bit packing layers remap some outlier activations; when we write/read cached KV blocks we apply a different packed ordering that creates bit-level discrepancies for rare tokens. Prefetch exacerbates because it writes precomputed packed blocks before runtime path completes remap checks.
2) Race between prefetch writer and runtime resharder (less likely): prefetch writes blocks earlier; if runtime applies final remap/transpose later the stored layout mismatches read layout.
3) Microbatch reordering: batching reorder policy with short latency windows may be replaying token ids in an unexpected order for 4-bit, exposing a latent indexing bug.

Immediate actions (owners + ETA):
- Disable prefetch for hawthorn-7b default profile in dedicated-n1 pools until a patch (temporary safety). Owner: Priya (actioned 2029-06-18).
- Add checksum-on-write + read-verify for KV cache in quant path (cheap guard) to detect and auto-invalidate suspect blocks. Owner: Lukas; prototype by 2029-06-21.
- Run focused ablation: 4-bit packing v1 vs v2, prefetch on/off, microbatch on/off across the failing testset (10k requests). Owner: Ethan; results by 2029-06-20.
- Add deterministic repro harness: 25-seed replay for multi-turn pronoun resolution examples (to capture drift). Owner: Maya; due 2029-06-20.
- Postmortem kickoff if checksum still triggered after above.

Short experiment plan (Ethan notes):
- Matrix: packing-profile {v1, v2, v2-remap-fix}, prefetch {on, off}, microbatch {on(8,5ms), off}. 2k requests per cell across convo-robustness-small. Measure TER, perplexity, p50/p95 latency, kv-checksum-fail.
- Quick perf expectation: packing-profile v2-remap-fix should match baseline TER if hypothesis 1 is correct.

Triage logs / quick debug artifacts:
- Example failure (abbreviated):
  - prompt: "User: Where did Maya leave the keys?\n    Assistant: She left them on the kitchen table.\n    User: What color were they?"
  - baseline: "They were silver."
  - 4bit-prefetch: "They were red." (inconsistent pronoun resolution)
  - debug: kv-checksum mismatch for block id 0x7a9c; write-timestamp 13:24:02.314

Notes from Lukas (implementation quick notes):
- Packing v2 uses chunked nibble layout with remap map R; current cache serializer assumes contiguous nibble ordering (legacy). Prefetch path uses serializer V1 by mistake for some code paths. Looks like a simple codepath mismatch (serializer versioning missing).
- Will add metadata header in cache blob with serializer version and simple CRC. If mismatch, invalidation and regen.

Blocking / questions:
- Do we want to auto-roll back existing dedicated slots that used default profile? (Risk: small unless workload hit) -> Decision: for now do not auto-rollback; disable prefetch only.
- How to instrument user-facing metrics to detect this type of drift early in hosted run? We should add a lightweight "context-stable" probe in eval harness that runs on a tiny sample of sessions and compares last-turn logits with baseline for divergence. Owner: Product/Optimize sync to discuss.

Follow-ups and timeline:
- 2029-06-18: prefetch disabled for hawthorn-7b default profile (Priya) - DONE
- 2029-06-20: deterministic repro harness + Ethan's ablation results - IN PROGRESS
- 2029-06-21: checksum guard prototype in quant cache (Lukas) - WIP
- 2029-06-22: decision meeting with runtime & infra to evaluate rollout of serializer header + auto-invalidate (scheduled 11:00 PT). Attendees: Maya, Lukas, Priya, Ethan, Noor, runtime eng lead.

Loose ideas (brainstorm):
- Make prefetch writer more conservative for quantized blobs: write only when sequence length > threshold or when auto-verified by runtime step.
- Maintain a tiny (8-byte) fingerprint per cached block computed from raw fp32 before quantization so we can cheaply detect structural divergence later without full CRC overhead.
- Add an on-deploy integration test that replays 100 multi-turn examples through new serializer/packing to catch this class of mismatch.

Notes to self (Maya):
- This is a good reminder: serialization versioning is cheap insurance. Add to onboarding checklist.
- Tie a small eval probe (10 sessions) to onboarding flow for any quant profile changes — if divergence > threshold, fail the rollout.

Open action list (short):
- [Priya] Disable prefetch for default profiles (done).
- [Ethan] Run full ablation matrix; collect metrics (due 6/20).
- [Lukas] Add serializer header + CRC and quick invalidation path (prototype 6/21).
- [Maya] Create onboarding checklist PR and add eval probe hook (6/20).
- [Noor] Prep runtime meeting notes and capacity impact estimate for disabling prefetch (6/21).

Quick decisions made in-standup:
- No customer rollback yet; prefer targeted config change (prefetch off) + quick guard.
- Prioritize checksum guard over full serializer refactor for immediate mitigation.

Misc capture (random):
- Found a related TODO in GH PR 4132: "align serializer versions in prefetch module" — flagged PR to patch.
- Minor: we should update docs in Confluence to explicitly call out serializer version in cache design doc.

If there are blockers or you want a deep-dive, ping in #applied-ml-quant and add "FRICTION" to the thread title.

-- end of quick standup capture --
